question.text: A piece of granite floats at the interface of mercury and water contained in a beaker as in figure. If the densities of granite, water and mercury are $\rho, \rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ respectively, the ratio of the volume of granite in water to the volume of granite in mercury is

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & V_1 \rho_1 g+V_2 \rho_2 g=V \rho g \\ & \Rightarrow V_1 \rho_1 g+V_2 \rho_2 g=\left(V_1+V_2\right) \rho g \\ & \Rightarrow V_1 \rho_1 g-V_1 \rho g=V_2 \rho g-V_2 \rho_2 g, \Rightarrow V_1\left(\rho-\rho_1\right)=V_2\left(\rho_2-\rho\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{\rho_{2-} \rho}{\rho-\rho_1}\end{aligned}$
